text:
Sarah M: quick RFC follow-up — I'm trying to pick between adding short-lived allocation leases vs relying on a passive background defragger for our fragmentation pain. thoughts?

Raj P: can you sketch the failure modes you're worried about?

Sarah M: mainly: tail-latency spikes when many small tensors cause scatter across slabs, and long GC pauses when we run a global compact. leases might let us pin work in-place and coordinate handoffs. passive defrag is simpler but less deterministic.

Anika V: Agree. Two tradeoffs: predictability (leases win) vs complexity + cross-node coordination (leases lose). Also leases need a reclaim path if a runner dies.

Kevin T: curious about API surface — if we add leases, allocator becomes stateful. Example proto:```
// sketch
interface Allocator {
  AcquireLease(alloc_id) -> lease_id | error
  ReleaseLease(lease_id) -> ok
  TrySteal(lease_id_parent) -> lease_id_child | null
  HintDefrag(region_id, urgency)
}
```
That lets callers express intent.

Liam G: what about partial strategy: leases for hot allocations (long-lived, high-reuse), passive defrag for cold churn?

Sarah M: exactly what I was thinking — need a hot/cold classifier. We already have hot-score telemetry; could feed that into lease decisions.

Raj P: how do leases interact with eviction and host-staging? if a lease keeps a slab pinned, we might block necessary offload, increasing OOM risk.

Anika V: two policies: "soft lease" (lease is advisory, allocator can preempt with a callback) vs "hard lease" (prevents eviction until explicit release). Soft lease seems safer for multi-tenant hosts.

Kevin T: soft lease means we need a callback path and backoff semantics. e.g.,`OnPreempt(lease_id) -> grace_ms` so the holder can either checkpoint or migrate.

Sarah M: sketching cost model: leasing adds RPC/coordination cost on Acquire/Release. Passive defrag adds continuous CPU background cost and periodic latency hits during compacts. Which is cheaper depends on hotset fraction.

Liam G: we can simulate quickly using current telemetry. I can run a strawman: assume 10% hot allocations, lease ops 200ns local + 1ms for cross-node coordinator, defrag sweep costs 50ms/host once per 30s.

Raj P: don't forget tenant fairness — leases could be hogged by noisy apps unless we add quotas or lease TTLs.

Anika V: Lease TTL + renewal solves that. Also add metrics: `lease_acquires`, `lease_preempts`, `defrag_runs`, `compaction_pauses_ms`. We'll need SLO alerts.

Kevin T: implementation surface: 1) local-only leases (no cross-node state) are cheap but won't help multi-GPU tensors, 2) cluster leases require a lease manager (etcd-ish?) or piggyback on existing control-plane. I'd prefer piggyback to avoid new dependencies.

Sarah M: piggybacking on control-plane likely fine for Dedicated, but Hosted low-latency path shouldn't pay round-trips. maybe hybrid: local fast-path + eventual sync to control-plane for visibility.

Liam G: what about a downgrade path: if node is under memory pressure, auto-convert soft leases to preemptible with shorter grace, then migrate. Need clear signal channels.

Raj P: signal could be existing residency/vram_pressure metric. preemption sequence: signal -> grace -> snapshot/migrate -> release. document sequence in allocator contract.

Anika V: also think about testing: we should add a fault-injection harness that kills holders mid-lease to validate reclaim logic. Postmortem from last week highlights we didn't test that enough.

Kevin T: API backwards-compat: keep current `Alloc`/`Free` and add `Lease*` as opt-in. callers that don't opt-in get passive defrag behavior.

Sarah M: good. action items: 1) Liam run sim on telemetry, 2) Anika propose metrics + TTL/default policy, 3) Kevin prototype local lease fast-path and `OnPreempt` callback contract. I'll synthesize into RFC follow-up next week.

devops-bot: deployment: allocator-service v0.0.0-rc1 scheduled to canary in staging at 2026-03-22T04:00:00Z :robot_face: 

Raj P: one more: think through quota evictions for Dedicated customers — leases should be tied to tenant quotas so they can't bypass reservation limits.

Sarah M: yes. tie lease grants to quota checks. thanks everyone — I'll write up a concise decision matrix and queue RFC edits. :thumbsup:
